key_insight: Diffusion-DRF introduces a differentiable reward flow that lets preference signals be propagated as gradients through the video diffusion process, enabling direct fine-tuning of T2V models without relying on non-differentiable rewards or heavy human labeling.
problem_solved: Current T2V fine-tuning relies on non-differentiable preference signals (human annotations or learned reward models), which are label-intensive, prone to bias and reward hacking, and lead to unstable training.
method: Construct a differentiable reward flow that converts preference signals into continuous, backpropagatable guidance for video diffusion denoising steps.
Fine-tune the diffusion model by propagating reward gradients through the sampling/denoising chain (while keeping the reward evaluator stable/frozen), avoiding discrete preference optimization.
Incorporate regularization and smoothing in the reward flow to reduce reward hacking and stabilize training with fewer annotated labels.
impact: Enables more sample-efficient, stable, and robust fine-tuning of video diffusion models for improved visual fidelity and text alignment, reducing dependence on costly human labels and brittle reward functions.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: input prompt → video diffusion model → differentiable reward flow → gradient backpropagation to model

Bar chart or icon set: fewer labels required, reduced reward hacking incidents, improved fidelity/alignment metrics (conceptual)
paper_title: Diffusion-DRF: Differentiable Reward Flow for Video Diffusion Fine-Tuning
paper_authors: Yifan Wang, Yanyu Li, Sergey Tulyakov, Yun Fu, Anil Kag
